oewn-01159815-v.learner: to use up resources or materials.
examples: The old car eats a lot of petrol on long trips.

oewn-01770125-v.learner: to keep worrying someone or making them anxious.
examples: Something was eating him, but he would not say what it was.

oewn-00275082-v.learner: to make something get worse or break down through the action of water, air, or an acid.
examples: The acid ate through the metal pipe.

oewn-01422127-v.learner: to change how something is arranged or where it is.
examples: Strong winds vexed the surface of the sea.

oewn-00814544-v.learner: to examine, discuss, or think about something for a long time.
examples: Scholars have vexed the question for many years without agreeing.

oewn-01499136-v.learner: to put things in a certain order or arrangement.
examples: She disposed the chairs in a circle around the fire.

oewn-00301542-v.learner: to make someone or something fit or ready.
examples: Good food and a night's rest disposed the troops for the long march.

oewn-00082316-v.learner: to bring help or ease to someone or something in trouble.
examples: it has often led him to be liberal and generous; to give his money freely, to display hospitality, to assist his tenants, and relieve the poor.

oewn-02417305-v.learner: to free someone from their duties for a period of time.
examples: At midnight another guard came to relieve him.

oewn-00895399-v.learner: to excuse or release someone from something.
examples: A note from the doctor relieved her from sports for a week.

oewn-02570061-v.learner: to let someone off from following a rule or meeting a requirement.
examples: Poor farmers were relieved from paying the new tax.

oewn-00199442-v.learner: to lessen or remove pressure or stress, or to make something less hard to bear.
examples: A valve in the pipe relieves the pressure when it gets too high.

oewn-02556565-v.learner: to save something from being ruined, destroyed, or harmed.
examples: An army marched north to relieve the town under siege.
A pickpocket relieved him of his wallet on the train.

connotation.why: polite-sounding word used in place of steal

oewn-00938680-v.learner: to free yourself of troubling information by telling it to someone.
examples: She relieved herself of the secret by telling her sister everything.

oewn-02270824-v.learner: to put money aside so that you have it to use later.
examples: She saves ten dollars every week for a new bike.

oewn-02271765-v.learner: to spend less money, or to pay a lower price for something.
examples: You save twenty percent if you buy the tickets online.

oewn-02557529-v.learner: to bring someone or something into a safe place or state.
examples: The captain saved the crew by steering the ship into the harbour.

oewn-02470006-v.learner: to choose not to hurt someone or something.
examples: The hunter saved the young deer and let it run away.

oewn-02557299-v.learner: to free someone from their sins.
examples: They believed that faith would save their souls.

oewn-01000931-v.learner: to store information on a computer.
examples: Save the file before you close the program.

oewn-02288561-v.learner: to keep your right to have or use something.
examples: Could you save my place in the queue while I get a drink?

oewn-01045759-v.learner: to make a whining, ringing, or whistling sound.
examples: The kettle sang on the stove.
A stone sang past his head.

oewn-00750606-s.learner: hard to deal with and needing great care not to upset anyone.
examples: And, if I may mention so delicate a subject, endeavour to check that little something, bordering on conceit and impertinence, which your lady possesses.

oewn-00712660-s.learner: easy to break, damage, or destroy.
examples: Be careful with that glass vase; it is very delicate.

oewn-00709335-a.learner: very fine, subtle, and pleasing, and also easily harmed.
examples: She served the tea in delicate china cups.
Use a mild soap on a baby's delicate skin.

oewn-01955211-s.learner: made or worked out in a very fine and subtle way.
examples: The characteristics of Miss Austen's humour are so subtle and delicate that they are, perhaps, at all times easier to apprehend than to express

oewn-02111262-s.learner: of a tool or device: able to measure very small differences or changes exactly.
examples: Only a very delicate instrument could detect such a small change.
Mr. Philips visited them all, and this opened to his nieces a source of felicity unknown before.
The cause of the fire is still unknown.
The film starred an unknown young actor.

oewn-00121594-s.learner: coming from someone or something whose name is not known or not given.
examples: The money was given by an unknown donor.

oewn-02379193-s.learner: not known to be there at all.
examples: The divers found a kind of fish unknown to science.

oewn-00291174-r.learner: in a short way, using only a few words.
examples: These causes must be stated, though briefly.
To Mr. Bennet's acknowledgments he briefly replied, with assurances of his eagerness to promote the welfare of any of his family
We met briefly last summer.

oewn-00350856-n.learner: the act of changing direction, or of going back the opposite way.
examples: The turning of the big ship took several minutes.

oewn-07366212-n.learner: a movement in a new direction.
examples: The sudden turning of the wind blew smoke into our faces.

oewn-00196264-n.learner: the act of changing the way things are usually done.
examples: The town's turning away from its old customs was slow.

oewn-00927993-n.learner: the work of shaping something on a lathe, a machine that spins it while it is cut.
examples: He learned wood turning at evening classes.

oewn-04507799-n.learner: an object made by shaping something on a lathe.
examples: The shop sold bowls and other wooden turnings.

oewn-09487228-n.learner: a thin piece that comes off when something is shaped on a lathe.
examples: Metal turnings piled up on the floor under the lathe.
